Start: ^[An elderly man stands near the graveyard, his gaze fixed on a single weathered gravestone. His shoulders are heavy, as if bearing the weight of years of grief. He doesn’t look up as you approach.]
^[[Elderly Man]]: You’ve come to this place, drawn like the others. The forest brought you, didn’t it?
^No, I came of my own choice.
Option_Brought: ^[[Elderly Man]]: No one comes here by chance. The forest has a way of calling to those with questions it might answer, or fears it might exploit.
^My name is Victor. I’ve seen many come and go, drawn by the same pull. Perhaps you’ll find what you seek, though I wouldn’t trust what it offers.
Option_Choice: ^[[You]]: No, I came of my own choice.
^[[Elderly Man]]: [Chuckles softly.] That’s what we all think, at first. But the forest… it whispers, even when we can’t hear it. You wouldn’t be here unless it wanted you to be.
^I’m Victor. Remember the name if the forest doesn’t take you first.
Option_WhyHere: ^[[Elderly Man]]: [Pauses, his voice heavy.] I stand here because she lies there. My wife. Two years gone.
^I’m Victor. I’ve stood here every day since, watching over her. The forest took her, like it takes everything in the end.
AfterIntroduction: ^[[Victor]]: You’ve seen the town, haven’t you? It’s a hollow shell. Families torn apart. Lives lost. That forest… it doesn’t just kill; it unravels us.
^You seem to blame it for everything.
Option_Take: ^[[Victor]]: It’s not just the wolves ors. It’s the way it seeps into you, plants its roots in your soul. It finds your weakness and pulls.
^For my wife, it was her dreams. She thought she could escape. She thought it whispered promises… but it lied.
Option_Blame: ^[[You]]: You seem to blame it for everything.
^[[Victor]]: [Laughs bitterly.] Wouldn’t you? The forest is no mere place. It’s a predator. It takes what it wants, and it never gives it back.
^My family… my wife… the forest tore them apart, just like it’s torn this town to shreds.
Option_Sorry: ^[[Victor]]: [Nods slowly.] We all lose something here. Some lose their lives, others their hope. But thank you. It’s not often anyone stops to say that.
End: ^Be careful, stranger. The forest has taken more than you can imagine, and it’s always hungry for more.
^[He turns back to the gravestone, his hand resting gently on its weathered surface.]
^I’ll stay here a while longer. You go on. Just… don’t let it take you too.
